name: Tomato Bacterial Wilt
description: A destructive soil-borne bacterial disease causing rapid wilting and death of tomato plants. It is widespread in tropical regions including Nigeria, and affects a wide range of crops in the solanaceae family.
symptoms: Sudden wilting of leaves starting from younger leaves during heat of day
Bacterial ooze visible when cut stem is placed in water
Roots appearing healthy while vascular tissue is degraded
causes: Soil-borne pathogen surviving in soil for years
High soil moisture and poor drainage
Root damage from transplanting or weeding
treatments: No effective chemical cure once plants are infected
Remove and destroy infected plants with surrounding soil
Apply lime to affected areas to raise soil pH
Solarize soil during hot dry season
prevention: Use grafted tomato plants onto resistant rootstocks
Practice long crop rotation (4+ years) with non-solanaceous crops
Plant in well-drained fields or raised beds
Use resistant tomato varieties where available
Disinfect tools and equipment between fields
Avoid planting in fields with history of bacterial wilt
